q: Are the portfolio examples verified client case studies?
a: The detailed examples here are illustrative SEO strategies, not verified client-result reports. The 10+ project count was supplied by Shobon; specific client metrics are not published without source data.

q: Why are exact traffic growth percentages not shown?
a: A reliable percentage needs a defined baseline, date range and analytics source. Publishing a number without those would mislead readers, so these pages explain the approach and what would be measured.

q: What does an SEO project usually include?
a: A project can include a technical audit, intent-led keyword research, page architecture, content briefs, internal linking and reporting. Scope follows the biggest constraint on qualified search growth.
Compare organic search data and conversions against a documented baseline. Separate branded from non-branded demand and note seasonality, site changes and other marketing activity.

q: Can you work with a confidential client?
a: Yes. A project can be discussed without naming the company, but any published results should still be approved and supported by evidence.

q: Which industries can your SEO approach support?
a: The frameworks shown cover SaaS, health technology, legal technology, logistics, design and e-commerce. Each market still needs its own customer research and search analysis.

q: Can I request a strategy for my own website?
a: Yes. Share your website, goals and current challenge through the contact page. A first review can identify whether technical issues, missing pages or conversion friction deserve priority.

q: Does an example strategy guarantee the same result?
a: No. Results depend on the site's starting point, competition, execution and time. Examples explain decisions, not a promise of rankings or leads.
